findings.issue_text: Duplicate group-key safety net removed in StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate: results[result.group_key] = result silently overwrites duplicates instead of logging an error and skipping, and the corresponding test test_state_results_multi_group_dupe was deleted rather than adapted

PriorityLevel(new_status) cast assumes DetectorPriorityLevel and PriorityLevel share identical enum values for all non-OK levels; a mismatch would raise ValueError in the evaluation hot path, dropping the entire data packet's results

MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but does not implement the abstract methods get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data, so instantiating it raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class, breaking processing for any detector with a metric-alert grouptype slug

Unbounded per-packet fan-out of occurrence production: get_group_key_values returns the packet's dict with no cap on group keys, and process_detectors emits one Kafka produce per transitioning key, so large subscriber-derived packets can trigger a burst of occurrence builds and Kafka messages; repeated flapping transitions across many keys re-amplifies
detector.group_type registry lookup repeated per result construction: the property calls grouptype.registry.get_by_slug on every access instead of being cached by the handler

Tautological occurrence assertions: tests verify the mock handler against itself since build_mock_occurrence_and_event is used both as the mock implementation and to build expected values, validating only wiring and not correctness of occurrence construction (fingerprint, detection_time, priority, project_id)

Duplicate-group-key guard removed with no replacement: old code logged an error and skipped duplicate group_keys; new dict-based evaluate silently overwrites with last-write-wins, producing only one Kafka occurrence, and the defensive test was deleted rather than adapted with no new coverage

TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected occurrence for the wrong group key: build_mock_occurrence_and_event is called with "val1" while expected_result.group_key is "group_key", so the fixture is mismatched and the assertion can't be verifying what it appears to verify

No process-level test for the resolve (OK) path producing a StatusChangeMessage to Kafka: process-level tests only exercise the occurrence branch and assert status_change=None; the StatusChangeMessage routing branch in process_detectors is untested in this PR

test_state_results_multi_group builds occurrence_2 with wrong value: built with value 6 while the packet value for group_2 is 10, and the mismatch is invisible because the same stub builds both sides, leaving the value argument untested end-to-end

PriorityLevel(new_status) casts DetectorPriorityLevel to issues-domain PriorityLevel purely by numeric value across distinct enums with no guaranteed value alignment, risking wrong severity or ValueError in the hot evaluation path; mapping should be explicit

Duplicate group keys from handlers are now silently deduplicated via dict-based return, removing the old 'Duplicate detector state group keys found' logging, so one result is silently discarded (last write wins) and the underlying handler bug is hidden

build_occurrence_and_event_data added as @abc.abstractmethod on StatefulDetectorHandler makes MetricAlertDetectorHandler (which is an empty stub subclass) fail with TypeError on instantiation, breaking registry lookup paths for MetricAlertDetectionType at runtime
Dead/empty setUp override in TestProcessDetectors that only calls super().setUp() is minor dead code in tests

Silent overwrite of duplicate group keys: duplicate-key error log guard was removed and replaced with `results[result.group_key] = result`, so duplicates silently collapse (last write wins) and detections can vanish without trace; the deleted dupe test also removes regression signal (src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py, StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate ~line 240-248)

Occurrences attributed to hardcoded project_id = 1: `Detector.project_id` property returns literal 1 and is now consumed by `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, so all metric-alert IssueOccurrences would be created in project 1, misattributing issues and likely breaking group resolution/status changes (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:58)

`PriorityLevel(new_status)` cast can raise ValueError: DetectorPriorityLevel and PriorityLevel are separate enums with independent values; value-based lookup will throw at evaluation time if values diverge, killing the whole detector batch, with no mapping/translation function and tests only exercising HIGH (src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py, evaluate_group_key_value ~line 299)

Tautological test fixtures mask incorrect value propagation: tests rebuild expected occurrences using the same helper as the handler mock and value isn't embedded in the mock occurrence, so tests pass even with wrong value/timestamp/fingerprint inputs (tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py, test_state_results_multi_group, TestEvaluate)

Occurrence produced to Kafka before state commit: `process_detectors` produces occurrences to Kafka while `commit_state_updates` happens afterwards, creating a partial-failure/duplicate window (re-firing duplicates if commit fails after produce; lost alerts if commit succeeds but produce throws) with no idempotency key tying Kafka payload to committed state version

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate group-key safety net removed in StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate: results[result.group_key] = result silently overwrites duplicates instead of logging an error and skipping, and the corresponding test test_state_results_multi_group_dupe was deleted rather than adapted

adjudication.rationale: The old duplicate-safety code in `process_detectors` only made sense when `handler.evaluate()` returned a *list* of `DetectorEvaluationResult` objects that could contain the same `group_key` multiple times. This diff changes the contract so `DetectorHandler.evaluate` returns a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` (see signature change and call site iterating `detector_results.values()`), and `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` builds that dict from `group_values`, which itself is a dict (`get_group_key_values(...) -> dict[str, int]`). With dict-based inputs/outputs, duplicate group keys are not representable in the same way, so there is no verifiable “silent overwrite” defect here; the removed dupe test was tied to list-based duplicates (`group_keys=["dupe","dupe"]`) which no longer matches the API (`group_vals` is a dict).

adjudication_records.issue_text: PriorityLevel(new_status) cast assumes DetectorPriorityLevel and PriorityLevel share identical enum values for all non-OK levels; a mismatch would raise ValueError in the evaluation hot path, dropping the entire data packet's results

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `PriorityLevel(new_status)` in `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value` when `new_status` is a `DetectorPriorityLevel` (non-OK path). If those enums’ underlying values don’t align, this will raise `ValueError` and there’s no local handling, so processing would fail for that packet. However, the diff does not show the definitions/values of `DetectorPriorityLevel` vs `PriorityLevel`, so an actual mismatch (and thus a guaranteed defect) can’t be verified from the diff alone—only the risk/assumption is evident.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but does not implement the abstract methods get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data, so instantiating it raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class, breaking processing for any detector with a metric-alert grouptype slug

Unbounded per-packet fan-out of occurrence production: get_group_key_values returns the packet's dict with no cap on group keys, and process_detectors emits one Kafka produce per transitioning key, so large subscriber-derived packets can trigger a burst of occurrence builds and Kafka messages; repeated flapping transitions across many keys re-amplifies

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate()` iterating over every entry returned by `get_group_key_values()` (`for group_key, group_value in group_values.items():`) and, on non-OK transitions, calling `build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` to produce an occurrence per transitioning key. `process_detectors()` then iterates `detector_results.values()` and calls `create_issue_occurrence_from_result(result)` for each, which (per tests) leads to one `produce_occurrence_to_kafka(...)` per result. There is no cap/batching in this flow, so a packet with many group keys can cause a burst of occurrence building and Kafka produces. This is a scalability/architecture concern grounded in the new stateful handler’s per-key evaluation pattern, not a strictly verifiable correctness bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: detector.group_type registry lookup repeated per result construction: the property calls grouptype.registry.get_by_slug on every access instead of being cached by the handler

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Detector.group_type` as a property that does `grouptype.registry.get_by_slug(self.type)` on each access (see `models/detector.py`). It is then used at least in `Detector.detector_handler` (`group_type = self.group_type`) and in test helper code (`handler.detector.group_type`). There is no caching/memoization shown, so repeated accesses will repeat the registry lookup. This is a real, diff-grounded performance/architecture concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tautological occurrence assertions: tests verify the mock handler against itself since build_mock_occurrence_and_event is used both as the mock implementation and to build expected values, validating only wiring and not correctness of occurrence construction (fingerprint, detection_time, priority, project_id)

adjudication.rationale: In tests, the mock stateful handler’s implementation of `build_occurrence_and_event_data` directly delegates to `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(...)` (see `MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data`). The expected values in multiple assertions are also constructed by calling the same `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(...)` helper (e.g., `test_state_results`, `test_state_results_multi_group`, `TestEvaluate.*`). This makes the assertions largely tautological: they confirm that the handler returns/produces whatever `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` builds, but they don’t independently validate occurrence construction details like fingerprint composition, `detection_time`, `initial_issue_priority`, or `project_id` correctness beyond that shared helper’s behavior. This is a test-quality/design concern, not a runtime defect shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate-group-key guard removed with no replacement: old code logged an error and skipped duplicate group_keys; new dict-based evaluate silently overwrites with last-write-wins, producing only one Kafka occurrence, and the defensive test was deleted rather than adapted with no new coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the detector evaluation contract from `list[DetectorEvaluationResult]` to `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` (see `DetectorHandler.evaluate` / `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` signatures and `process_detectors` return type). With a dict, duplicate `group_key`s are not representable at the API boundary, so the old `set()`-based duplicate guard in `process_detectors` becomes redundant. Likewise, `StatefulDetectorHandler.get_group_key_values` returns a `dict[str, int]`, which also cannot contain duplicate keys. The removed "dupe" test relied on passing a list with duplicates (`group_keys=["dupe", "dupe"]`), but that input shape no longer exists. While `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` does assign into a dict (`results[result.group_key] = result`), the finding’s claim that this removal introduces a bug and reduces Kafka occurrences is not verifiable from the new interfaces shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected occurrence for the wrong group key: build_mock_occurrence_and_event is called with "val1" while expected_result.group_key is "group_key", so the fixture is mismatched and the assertion can't be verifying what it appears to verify

adjudication.rationale: In `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe`, the test constructs `expected_result` with `group_key="group_key"` but builds the `IssueOccurrence` via `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", ...)`. Since `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` uses `handler.build_fingerprint(group_key)`, the occurrence’s fingerprint (and thus the `IssueOccurrence`) is tied to "val1" rather than "group_key", so the expected fixture is inconsistent with the group key under test and would either make the assertion incorrect or cause a failure depending on equality semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No process-level test for the resolve (OK) path producing a StatusChangeMessage to Kafka: process-level tests only exercise the occurrence branch and assert status_change=None; the StatusChangeMessage routing branch in process_detectors is untested in this PR

adjudication.rationale: In `process_detectors`, results are now iterated as a dict (`for result in detector_results.values():`) and any non-None `result.result` is forwarded via `create_issue_occurrence_from_result(result)`. The stateful handler logic can produce either an `IssueOccurrence` (non-OK path via `build_occurrence_and_event_data`) or a `StatusChangeMessage` (OK path in `evaluate_group_key_value`, where `result = StatusChangeMessage(...)`). The updated process-level tests (`test_state_results` and `test_state_results_multi_group`) only patch/assert `produce_occurrence_to_kafka` calls for the occurrence branch with `status_change=None`, and there is no corresponding process-level test that drives `new_status == OK` and asserts the Kafka call for the `StatusChangeMessage` branch. Unit-level tests cover OK returning a `StatusChangeMessage`, but the process-level routing to Kafka is untested in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PriorityLevel(new_status) casts DetectorPriorityLevel to issues-domain PriorityLevel purely by numeric value across distinct enums with no guaranteed value alignment, risking wrong severity or ValueError in the hot evaluation path; mapping should be explicit

adjudication.rationale: In `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value`, the diff adds `PriorityLevel(new_status)` when calling `build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` (i.e., converting a `DetectorPriorityLevel` to `sentry.types.group.PriorityLevel` by enum value). The diff does not show any explicit mapping or guarantee that the two distinct enums share identical values, so this is a brittle coupling and could raise `ValueError` or produce an incorrect priority if the enums diverge. However, the diff alone does not prove the values are currently misaligned, so it’s a grounded design/correctness risk rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate group keys from handlers are now silently deduplicated via dict-based return, removing the old 'Duplicate detector state group keys found' logging, so one result is silently discarded (last write wins) and the underlying handler bug is hidden

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the explicit duplicate-group-key detection/logging in `process_detectors` (the `detector_group_keys` set and `logger.error("Duplicate detector state group keys found", ...)` block is deleted) and changes `DetectorHandler.evaluate`/`StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` to return a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`. In `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate`, results are accumulated via `results[result.group_key] = result`, so if duplicate keys are produced during construction, the last assignment wins with no log. This does reduce observability of that anomaly, but it also reflects the new API contract (a mapping implies unique keys), so it’s more of a diagnosability/contract change than a clear correctness bug in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent overwrite of duplicate group keys: duplicate-key error log guard was removed and replaced with `results[result.group_key] = result`, so duplicates silently collapse (last write wins) and detections can vanish without trace; the deleted dupe test also removes regression signal (src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py, StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate ~line 240-248)

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `DetectorHandler.evaluate` / `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` now returns a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` (not a list). For `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate`, the loop iterates over `group_values.items()`, and `group_values` comes from `get_group_key_values(...) -> dict[str, int]`, so duplicate group keys cannot be represented there in the first place. The prior duplicate-key guard/test relied on a list of group keys (e.g. `group_keys=["dupe","dupe"]`) which is no longer part of the API. While `results[result.group_key] = result` technically overwrites if the same key is assigned twice, the code shown cannot produce that situation given the dict-based inputs/iteration, so “detections can vanish without trace” isn’t verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Occurrences attributed to hardcoded project_id = 1: `Detector.project_id` property returns literal 1 and is now consumed by `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, so all metric-alert IssueOccurrences would be created in project 1, misattributing issues and likely breaking group resolution/status changes (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:58)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Detector.project_id` is hardcoded to `1` (with a TODO/XXX comment) and the new occurrence-building path for `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value` now requires concrete handlers to build an `IssueOccurrence` plus `event_data`. However, in this PR there is no production `build_occurrence_and_event_data` implementation (only test helper `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` uses `handler.detector.project_id`), and `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` is changed to `pass`, so the claim that “all metric-alert IssueOccurrences would be created in project 1” isn’t directly verifiable from the diff. What is verifiable is that the new API makes it easy for future/other handlers to rely on the placeholder `project_id`, which would misattribute occurrences if used as-is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `PriorityLevel(new_status)` cast can raise ValueError: DetectorPriorityLevel and PriorityLevel are separate enums with independent values; value-based lookup will throw at evaluation time if values diverge, killing the whole detector batch, with no mapping/translation function and tests only exercising HIGH (src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py, evaluate_group_key_value ~line 299)

adjudication.rationale: In `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value`, the new code calls `PriorityLevel(new_status)` where `new_status` is a `DetectorPriorityLevel` (from `sentry.workflow_engine.types`). This relies on the two enums being value-compatible; otherwise `Enum` construction can raise `ValueError`/fail at runtime. The diff shows no explicit mapping/translation layer between the enums, and the updated tests only exercise the `HIGH` path (so they don't prove other `DetectorPriorityLevel` members are safely convertible). This is a real robustness concern introduced by the change, but the diff alone doesn't prove the values currently diverge.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tautological test fixtures mask incorrect value propagation: tests rebuild expected occurrences using the same helper as the handler mock and value isn't embedded in the mock occurrence, so tests pass even with wrong value/timestamp/fingerprint inputs (tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py, test_state_results_multi_group, TestEvaluate)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the tests constructing expected occurrences via the same helper that the mock handler uses: `MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data()` delegates to `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(...)`, and the tests (e.g. `test_state_results_multi_group`, `TestEvaluate`) also call `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(...)` to create the expected `IssueOccurrence`/`event_data`. That helper does not incorporate the `value` into the `IssueOccurrence` or `event_data` (it only uses `group_key` for `fingerprint` and `new_status` for `initial_issue_priority`), so incorrect value propagation would not be detected. This is concretely visible in `test_state_results_multi_group`, where `group_vals` uses `"group_2": 10` but the expected occurrence for `group_2` is built with `value` hardcoded to `6`, and the test can still pass because `value` is unused.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Occurrence produced to Kafka before state commit: `process_detectors` produces occurrences to Kafka while `commit_state_updates` happens afterwards, creating a partial-failure/duplicate window (re-firing duplicates if commit fails after produce; lost alerts if commit succeeds but produce throws) with no idempotency key tying Kafka payload to committed state version

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate()` enqueues state updates via `enqueue_state_update(...)` (see `evaluate_group_key_value`) but does not commit them. Meanwhile `process_detectors()` immediately iterates `for result in detector_results.values():` and calls `create_issue_occurrence_from_result(result)` when `result.result is not None`, which (per tests added in this diff) triggers `produce_occurrence_to_kafka(...)`. The diff does not show any call to `handler.commit_state_updates()` inside `process_detectors()`, so producing to Kafka is not coupled to a durable state write in the same function. The reviewer’s point about a partial-failure/duplicate window is a valid architecture/consistency concern grounded in this ordering, but the diff alone doesn’t prove the overall pipeline commits state “afterwards” or lacks idempotency, so it’s not a verifiable defect from the shown changes.
